evidence: Checked the complete settled-input.md. (a) The equivalent mechanisms are present as 'normal bounded scan', 'due cursors', 'bounded indexed due discovery', historical 'materialize/index due work', scheduler tests, and ht-0lo.1.3's 'bounded warning burst'. These establish discovery ownership and bounded work, but none states a scan cadence, fair multi-batch progress rule, detection-lag bound, or a test asserting backlog progress independently of deferred native delivery. (b) The contract expressly permits delayed native key submission, while expressly retaining 'bounded deadline detection'; this exception cannot justify indefinitely delayed durable warning creation. A6 permits explicit progress-based extensions, not scanner starvation. (c) No supported backlog/load bound or exclusion of historical bursts is stated; upgrade bursts are explicitly in scope. An unlimited-load SLA would exceed what is reasonable here, but a stated finite operating assumption and a multi-batch progress test do not. (d) The gap affects the core promised bounded handoff outcome: send-anchored deadlines alone cannot establish when overdue warnings become durable when historical work spans scans. The finding therefore survives refutation as an unverified design assumption. Should-fix rather than Blocking: the artifact specifies indexed discovery and existing scanning, and does not demonstrate an actual starvation defect; establish the finite-load progress/latency contract and its test before relying on the bounded-time promise.
